title: Waikiki Beach disappoints, then shipped to Guam
summary: Waikiki looked worse than Jones Beach to Holmes, and orders sent the show on to Guam.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So we're lookin' the place the place over and one-thing-or-another. The hotel is nice. The next day, Sylvester says, "Charlie, let's go out to Waikiki Beach," and I said, "Okay." So he got four or five of us together, and we got a jeep, and we made our way to Waikiki Beach. I

don't know who found it. None of us had ever been there before. But we found our way around. So we're standing on the beach, Waikiki beach, and it didn't look like anything to me -- it looked terrible. I mean, it was just nothin'. I don't mean it was bombed-up or anything like that; there was nothing like that happened there. But the beach itself didn't look like anything to me. I've seen much better beaches right here in the States. Jones Beach, for instance, looked better than that did. I mean, that was a big disappointment, too, because I had always heard so much about it. So that was my first big disappointment in Honolulu.

Well, this is the second day we're there, and when we come back to the hotel, our orders were to leave immediately. So there was only about five or six of us, half of the show had come back. So Sylvester is trying to tell this Special Service Officer, "Well, we can't leave right now; half of my company is out in the street somewhere." We don't know where they are. So the Special Services Officer said, "Well, we'll put you all on a plane, and we'll send the rest of them when they come in. So, well, we had to settle for that.
Anyway, we were shipped out, and they shipped us to Guam. The next stop was Guam. We were just stopping over.
